_meta.what: Political and economic levers for the page's Conditions panel. Each effect is a multiplier on visitors or residents' spending, or a change in business costs as a share of revenue, relative to the calibrated year (2025). 'measured' effects come from data; 'SEED' effects are stated assumptions.
_meta.closure_response: Two-year closure odds are multiplied by exp(gamma x profit squeeze), the squeeze being extra costs plus lost gross margin as a share of revenue. SEED gamma = 40 (a squeeze of 1% of revenue raises the odds by about half): yearly closures in the Employment Inventory roughly doubled from 2016-2019 to 2022-2025 while the prime rate rose about 2.3 points (debt costs about 0.5% of revenue), but that period also had pandemic debts and CEBA repayments, so only part of the doubling is credited to rates.

today.as_of: October 2026 (Bank of Canada; Ontario minimum wage from October 2025)

interest_rate.sources: Debt 20% of revenue: SEED (prep/nfprep/survival.py DEBT_RATIO). Residents' spending -0.7% per point of prime rate: SEED, in the range of Bank of Canada estimates of how rate changes pass to consumption over a year or two.

tariffs.sources: US overnight visitors through Niagara fell to 0.873 of 2024 in 2025 (calendar year) (Statistics Canada 24-10-0053, measured); 'none' undoes that drop, 'escalation' repeats it (SEED). Canadians' trips to the US fell 30% in 2025 and they travelled at home; domestic visitors -5% if that unwinds, +3% if it deepens (SEED). Goods cost: counter-tariffs on US goods raise the cost of goods sold by about 2% in an escalation (SEED); removing them lowers it 1%.

exchange_rate.sources: US overnight visitors through Niagara against the US dollar's price in Canadian dollars, yearly 2000-2025 without 2020-22: elasticity 0.71 (correlation 0.35, 23 years; Statistics Canada 24-10-0053 and Bank of Canada IEXM0101/FXMUSDCAD, data/monthly_history_1972_2026.json). Monthly 2017-2026 gave 0.84. Canadians' own US trips move the other way (-1.0).

minimum_wage.sources: Share of a kind's wages that move with the minimum wage: SEED (prep/nfprep/survival.py). Wage costs from Statistics Canada industry benchmarks.

border.label: Passport-type border rule
border.headline: Tighter border documents: US visitors -15%
border.sources: June 2009 passport requirement at the land border (WHTI): US overnight visitors x0.872, same-day x0.819 in the following 12 months (measured, Niagara ports).

health.label: Health scare (SARS-like)
health.headline: Health scare: visitors stay away
health.sources: SARS 2003: US overnight visitors x0.655 in April-June, x0.76 for the year (measured, Niagara ports). Domestic x0.85 from the Niagara Parks Falls lot (2003 vehicles x0.813 of 2002) with the visitor mix (docs/parking_check.json); overseas SEED.

security.label: Security shock (9/11-like)
security.headline: Security shock: US day trips dip, overnight holds
security.sources: Year after 9/11: US overnight visitors x1.03, same-day x0.945 (measured); the mix gives about x0.98.

recession.label: Recession
recession.headline: Recession: residents and Canadian visitors spend less
recession.sources: Matches the outlook's low end for residents and domestic visitors (data/scenario_ranges.json, SEED).

gas.label: Gas price spike
gas.headline: Gas price spike: fewer drive-in day trips
gas.sources: SEED: most Canadian visitors drive in.

mat.label: Hotel tax up to 5%
mat.headline: Municipal accommodation tax rises to 5%
mat.sources: City of Niagara Falls by-law 2025-009: 4% from April 2026, 5% from April 2027 (measured policy); SEED: room-price elasticity gives about -0.5% visitors.
